teachingQuestion: Why does token-by-token decoding make KV sharing valuable, and what evidence limits the claim that more sharing is always better?
adjacentCaption: Why this appears here: slides 57-63 form one causal chain—serial decode repeatedly reads a growing KV cache, fewer KV heads reduce those bytes, and slide 63 bounds the systems argument with empirical quality evidence. This companion keeps that chain together rather than reintroducing MHA, MQA, and GQA as a glossary.
posterAlt: Two evidence cards under the heading quality is empirical: Shazeer 2019 shows the cited MQA rows changing perplexity from 29.9 to 30.2, while Ainslie 2023 is labeled low or no GQA hit in the cited comparisons; a footer says this is not a universal guarantee.
caveat: The declared KV-cache byte totals scale exactly with head count, head dimension, dtype size, sequence, layers, and batch. Realized latency also depends on kernels, batching, hardware, layout, and other memory traffic. Slide 63 quality observations are empirical and setting-specific.
